PLUGIN_FEATURE_AUDIO_EFFECT.doc: The CLAP plugin features and LV2 plugin classes that become the descriptor feature audio-effect: every kind of effect, a filter, a dynamics processor, a modulation or a space, and the channel-less roles of a processor (utility, mixing, mastering).
PLUGIN_FEATURE_AUDIO_EFFECT.why: The four feature words stay; every CLAP plugin feature and LV2 plugin class is mapped onto them, or onto other, as data (FreeMixer/omx-contract#120). One item per target, so a word is the source term and is named once; a test holds the five items to the terms.

text.en: The CLAP plugin feature audio-effect: any audio effect with no more specific feature declared.
The CLAP plugin feature chorus: an effect that thickens a sound with detuned, delayed copies of it.
The CLAP plugin feature compressor: an effect that narrows a sound's dynamic range.
The CLAP plugin feature de-esser: an effect that tames sibilance in a voice.
The CLAP plugin feature delay: an effect that repeats a sound after a gap.
The CLAP plugin feature distortion: an effect that adds harmonics by overdriving a sound.
The CLAP plugin feature equalizer: an effect that shapes a sound's frequency balance.
The CLAP plugin feature expander: an effect that widens a sound's dynamic range.
The CLAP plugin feature filter: an effect that removes or shapes a band of frequencies.
The CLAP plugin feature flanger: an effect that sweeps a short, modulated delay against the dry sound.
The CLAP plugin feature frequency-shifter: an effect that shifts every frequency of a sound by the same amount.
The CLAP plugin feature gate: an effect that mutes a sound below a level.
The CLAP plugin feature glitch: an effect that cuts, stutters or corrupts a sound on purpose.
The CLAP plugin feature granular: an effect built from short grains of a sound.
The CLAP plugin feature limiter: an effect that holds a sound under a ceiling.
The CLAP plugin feature mastering: an effect meant for a mix's final stage.
The CLAP plugin feature mixing: an effect meant for use while mixing, such as a channel strip.
The CLAP plugin feature multi-effects: several effects combined in one plugin.
The CLAP plugin feature phase-vocoder: an effect built on a phase vocoder, typically to stretch or shift a sound independently of pitch and time.
The CLAP plugin feature phaser: an effect that sweeps notches through a sound with an all-pass filter chain.
The CLAP plugin feature pitch-correction: an effect that pulls a sound's pitch toward a scale.
The CLAP plugin feature pitch-shifter: an effect that changes a sound's pitch without changing its duration.
The CLAP plugin feature restoration: an effect that removes noise, clicks or other damage from a recording.
The CLAP plugin feature reverb: an effect that adds the reflections of a space to a sound.
The CLAP plugin feature transient-shaper: an effect that reshapes a sound's attack and sustain.
The CLAP plugin feature tremolo: an effect that modulates a sound's level over time.
The CLAP plugin feature utility: a plugin that does audio housekeeping rather than a creative effect.
The LV2 plugin class AllpassPlugin: an all-pass filter, which shifts phase without changing level.
The LV2 plugin class AmplifierPlugin: a plugin that changes a sound's level.
The LV2 plugin class BandpassPlugin: a filter that passes one band of frequencies.
The LV2 plugin class ChorusPlugin: an effect that thickens a sound with detuned, delayed copies of it.
The LV2 plugin class CombPlugin: a comb filter, which adds a short delayed copy of a sound to itself.
The LV2 plugin class CompressorPlugin: an effect that narrows a sound's dynamic range.
The LV2 plugin class ConverterPlugin: a plugin that converts a signal from one representation to another.
The LV2 plugin class DelayPlugin: an effect that repeats a sound after a gap.
The LV2 plugin class DistortionPlugin: an effect that adds harmonics by overdriving a sound.
The LV2 plugin class DynamicsPlugin: an effect that changes a sound's dynamic range.
The LV2 plugin class EQPlugin: an effect that shapes a sound's frequency balance.
The LV2 plugin class EnvelopePlugin: a plugin that follows or applies an envelope over time.
The LV2 plugin class ExpanderPlugin: an effect that widens a sound's dynamic range.
The LV2 plugin class FilterPlugin: an effect that removes or shapes a band of frequencies.
The LV2 plugin class FlangerPlugin: an effect that sweeps a short, modulated delay against the dry sound.
The LV2 plugin class GatePlugin: an effect that mutes a sound below a level.
The LV2 plugin class HighpassPlugin: a filter that passes frequencies above a cutoff.
The LV2 plugin class LimiterPlugin: an effect that holds a sound under a ceiling.
The LV2 plugin class LowpassPlugin: a filter that passes frequencies below a cutoff.
The LV2 plugin class MixerPlugin: a plugin that combines several signals into one.
The LV2 plugin class ModulatorPlugin: a plugin that modulates one signal with another.
The LV2 plugin class MultiEQPlugin: a multi-band equaliser.
The LV2 plugin class ParaEQPlugin: a parametric equaliser.
The LV2 plugin class PhaserPlugin: an effect that sweeps notches through a sound with an all-pass filter chain.
The LV2 plugin class PitchPlugin: a plugin that changes or tracks a sound's pitch.
The LV2 plugin class ReverbPlugin: an effect that adds the reflections of a space to a sound.
The LV2 plugin class SimulatorPlugin: a plugin that models a physical device or space.
The LV2 plugin class SpatialPlugin: a plugin that places or moves a sound in space.
The LV2 plugin class SpectralPlugin: a plugin that processes a sound in the frequency domain.
The LV2 plugin class UtilityPlugin: a plugin that does audio housekeeping rather than a creative effect.
The LV2 plugin class WaveshaperPlugin: a plugin that reshapes a waveform to add harmonics.

PLUGIN_FEATURE_INSTRUMENT.doc: The CLAP plugin features and LV2 plugin classes that become the descriptor feature instrument: notes in, audio out.

text.en: The CLAP plugin feature drum: an instrument that plays drum sounds.
The CLAP plugin feature drum-machine: an instrument that sequences and plays drum sounds.
The CLAP plugin feature instrument: a plugin played by notes, with no more specific kind declared.
The CLAP plugin feature sampler: an instrument that plays recorded samples.
The CLAP plugin feature synthesizer: an instrument that generates its own sound rather than playing samples.
The LV2 plugin class InstrumentPlugin: a plugin played by notes.

PLUGIN_FEATURE_NOTE_EFFECT.doc: The CLAP plugin features and LV2 plugin classes that become the descriptor feature note-effect: notes in, notes out.

text.en: The CLAP plugin feature note-effect: a plugin that reads notes and writes notes, such as an arpeggiator.
The LV2 plugin class MIDIPlugin: a plugin that processes MIDI, note in to note out.

PLUGIN_FEATURE_ANALYZER.doc: The CLAP plugin features and LV2 plugin classes that become the descriptor feature analyzer: audio in, a reading out (a note detector reads pitch from audio).

text.en: The CLAP plugin feature analyzer: a plugin that reads audio and reports a measurement, with no further output.
The CLAP plugin feature note-detector: an analyzer that reads pitch from audio.
The LV2 plugin class AnalyserPlugin: a plugin that reads audio and reports a measurement.

PLUGIN_FEATURE_OTHER.doc: The CLAP plugin features and LV2 plugin classes that fit none of the four feature words: a channel layout stated as a feature (mono, stereo, surround, ambisonic), and the LV2 classes of a generator, an oscillator, a constant and a function, which take no notes and so are no instrument. A scan carries them in the extension bag.

text.en: The CLAP plugin feature ambisonic: a plugin declared to work in an ambisonic channel layout.
The CLAP plugin feature mono: a plugin declared to work in a mono channel layout.
The CLAP plugin feature stereo: a plugin declared to work in a stereo channel layout.
The CLAP plugin feature surround: a plugin declared to work in a surround channel layout.
The LV2 plugin class ConstantPlugin: a plugin with no input that outputs a constant.
The LV2 plugin class FunctionPlugin: a plugin with no audio input or output, used only for its side effects or parameters.
The LV2 plugin class GeneratorPlugin: a plugin with no audio input that generates a sound.
The LV2 plugin class OscillatorPlugin: a generator that outputs a periodic waveform.
The LV2 plugin class Plugin: the base LV2 plugin class, with no more specific class declared.
